donor_structure: A firm holds an irreversible investment opportunity with sunk cost I and project value V following a stochastic process. Investing now kills the option to wait. Optimal policy is a stopping time: invest iff V crosses a hurdle V* > I; the wedge V* - I is the option value of waiting, increasing in volatility sigma and in irreversibility. Mean-collapse (invest iff E[V] >= I) is dominated for every sigma > 0 because the continuation value is convex in sigma.
target_structure: A_T11 at R5: module promotion criterion under uncertain future use (option-value form), assumption removal vi-fixed-ecology. Atom table has no verdict row for A_T11 (fully unrouted in D13). G16 scalar family (H_eff, C_build, C_maint, C_rev) provides the target quantities.
mapping: irreversible investment opportunity <-> promotion of a module from candidate to constituted (C_build sunk, demotion partial)
project value V <-> anticipated use intensity (H_eff process)
hurdle V* > I <-> promotion threshold on anticipated-use evidence strictly above renewal-reward breakeven
volatility sigma <-> use-process uncertainty (the vi removal)
value of waiting <-> keeping the module inline/unpromoted while evidence accumulates
smooth-pasting <-> threshold policy continuous in the evidence statistic (no bang-bang promotion at the boundary)
preserved_relations: promotion is a STOPPING DECISION on a filtered evidence process, not a one-shot expectation comparison
threshold sits strictly above mean breakeven; wedge increasing in uncertainty and irreversibility
mean-collapse criterion is dominated everywhere uncertainty > 0 (convexity of continuation value)
known_broken_relations: finance assumes a market price of risk/complete markets for the risk adjustment; HSG has no spanning market - the wedge must be derived from the process's own utility (fitness/burden), so only the STRUCTURE (not the pricing formula) transfers

Dixit-Pindyck value is continuous diffusion; module use evidence arrives as discrete events - cache-tiering promote-after-N is the discrete counting-instance (folded here as instance, see rejected list in log)

unknown_correspondences: closed form for h*(sigma, C_maint/C_build ratio, demotion recoverability fraction) under a compound-Poisson use process (vs geometric-Brownian V) - unmeasured
does the A_T05 saturation curve (A6-R0) interact with h*: promotion threshold at the saturation knee under uncertainty
assumptions_added: anticipated-use evidence admits a one-dimensional sufficient statistic (scalar stopping state)

candidate_theorem: The R5 module promotion criterion under uncertain future use is the optimal-stopping form: promote iff the anticipated-use statistic crosses h* strictly above the renewal-reward mean breakeven, with h* - breakeven nondecreasing in use-process uncertainty, in irreversibility, and in maintenance carry; the mean-collapse criterion (promote iff E[H_eff] clears breakeven) is dominated for every nonzero uncertainty. Discrete instance: promote-after-N evidence counting (cache tiering) is the memoryless-evidence special case.
strongest_parent: Dixit-Pindyck irreversible investment / optimal stopping (structure: stopping rule, hurdle wedge, waiting value)
proof_route: two-state example: H_eff in {low, high} with known transition rates, C_build=1, per-use saving s; solve the stopping problem exactly (Q-matrix) and exhibit h* > E[H_eff]-breakeven with wedge growing in the rate uncertainty; compare mean-collapse policy regret
